messages:
Sam K: incident-bot paged me: canary traffic shift reported elevated 5xx across 3 hosts in eu-west-1. healthcheck failure rate ~22% over 2m.
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] canary-failure eu-west-1 - 5xx spike. PagerDuty incident P12345 created and paged on-call.
Priya R: seeing a lot of 502/504 from fastpath on canary replica set rc-canary-47; nginx upstream timeout + grpc deadline exceeded in logs.
Marco L: FYI I increased rollout traffic from 10% -> 50% at 12:04 UTC to test throughput. rolled part of it back to 10% at 12:09 but errors kept climbing.
Lydia: quick check — are probes failing liveness or readiness? kubectl shows readiness=false for canary pods, restart count is 0.
Sam K: readiness failures (HTTP 200 -> 503 on /health). stack tracetips show kv cache misses and connection backlog. pod logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:06:11Z ERROR http: upstream timeout after 30s
2026-03-15T12:06:12Z WARN cache: eviction pressure, attempted alloc failed
```

Alex M: my recommendation: do NOT increase traffic to canary. Kill-switch the rollout flag and start rollback to last known good image (abc123). Scaling up canaries could just amplify the problem.
Priya R: +1. Plan: flip feature flag rollout.canary -> false (kill-switch), then trigger automated rollback to image abc123, recreate flapping pod(s).
Sam K: executing flag toggle now -> `/flags set rollout.canary false`
Marco L: saw the flag toggle, traffic redistributed back to stable pool in ~30s. monitoring shows 5xx rate drop from ~22% -> ~4% within 3m of toggle.
incident-bot: Action: flag rollout.canary disabled by Sam K. Automated rollback job queued (job id rb-1765).
Priya R: initiating rollback: `kubectl apply -f rollout-stable.yaml --record` -> rolling update to image abc123 across canary nodes.
Sam K: after rollback, most canary pods return 200 on /health. one pod (rc-canary-47-2) still has probe flapping, cordon + delete to force recreate.
Priya R: recreated pod rc-canary-47-2 -> readiness passing now. traces look normal.
Lydia: customer impact summary: ~1.2k failed requests (5xx) measured in eu-west-1 between 12:05-12:12 UTC. No cross-region impact observed. No SLO breach at org level but support should be notified for affected customers.
Marco L: opened support ticket RED-2026-301 and notified the customer success owner. https://support.example/ticket/RED-2026-301
Sam K: created incident thread in #incidents and pinned the mitigation notes. https://slack.com/archives/incidents/p1765554321
Alex M: handoff: I'm stepping away for ~20m. Priya, please take over monitoring and coordinate with eng-runtime for RCA.
Priya R: acknowledged — will run canary-evals, increase trace retention for the 12:00-12:30 window, and start draft RCA. hypothesis: kernel selection / quantized runtime mismatch under cache pressure + traffic burst.
Sam K: postmortem skeleton created: https://docs.internal/infra/incidents/1765554321 — add timeline and command outputs.
Priya R: assigned eng-runtime owners: Marco L and Alex M for deep dive on kernel/quantization paths and cache configuration. Also adding a regression test for kv-cache under concurrent load.
Sam K: closing active page (PagerDuty). If metrics re-escalate, re-pager. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident P12345 status: mitigated — follow-up tasks created (RCA, tests, support comms).
Priya R: handoff complete. last automated check at 12:25 UTC shows error rate stable ~0.5% in eu-west-1. I'll file full RCA + timeline by EOD and schedule a postmortem review.
Sam K: thanks all — quick timeline in case it helps: start rollout 12:04, error spike 12:06, flag off 12:12, rollback finish 12:15, mitigated 12:24. Handoff to Priya at 12:26.
